newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE may weaken to around 4,540.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE may weaken to around 4,540.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index will come under pressure on Tuesday, perhaps weaken to 4,540, technical amalysts said.
Despite recent losses -- the FTSE has dropped almost 110 points, or 2.3 percent over the past two days -- the market will have difficulty securing an area from which it can rebound, they added.
And with the index having been bashed down below 4,600 on Monday, market bears now have the psychological advantage and will be keen to exploit the situation further.
By 0707 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 2.9 at 4,559.9.
Technically, the damage was done once the 4,610 level crumbled yesterday and that action alone completed a bearish double top chart pattern on a line chart of the FTSE.
This pattern usually occurs towards the end of a bull run when share prices stumble but quickly find secondary buying interest to send prices higher once more.

But the buying pressure soon evaporates and sentiment changes which takes prices below previous support area where secondary buying interest had been shown. On a price chart this action appears as two adjacent peaks.
Loss of that key support area triggers off further selling.

The maximum height of the pattern when subtracted from the support area gives the next price target and from a line chart of the FTSE since mid-May, this downside target comes to 4,530, which may be reached in a few days.

Adding to the gloom is the current weakness on Wall Street where the Dow Jones industrial average has been making lower intra-day highs over the past few days and if this trend continues, the Dow could sink back to 7,210 over the near-term, analysts said.
On Monday, the Dow closed down 41.64 at 7,289.40.
